---
title: Execution records
---

## Overview

When Quarto runs the code in a document, it can keep what the code
produced --- each cell's outputs and each inline expression's value --- as an
**execution record**. A record lets Quarto present the document again
without running anything: `q2 preview` and hub use
this to show an up-to-date page while you edit prose.

A record is an ordinary Jupyter notebook file (`.ipynb`), whichever engine ran
the code, so other tools can read it. Each cell of the notebook is one
**unit** of the document: a code cell, or an inline expression.

::: callout-note
## Opt-in for now

A plain `q2 render` writes nothing under `.quarto/`. The preview keeps the
records it needs on its own. `record: true`, shown below, asks for a copy of
the record under the project's `.quarto/` directory. Hub uploads from
`q2 provide-hub` still use the older format unless you set the environment
variable `QUARTO_ENGINE_RECORD_WRITE` to `1`, while the feature is rolled out.
:::

## Keeping a copy of the record

Add `record: true` to the document's `execute` options:

````markdown
---
title: Report
jupyter: python3
execute:
  record: true
---
````

A render then also writes a copy of the record under the project's `.quarto/` directory, at
`.quarto/execution-records/<document path without extension>.ipynb`. In a
project, `reports/q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/reports/q3.ipynb`
at the project root. A standalone document with no project gets a `.quarto/`
beside it, so `q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/q3.ipynb`.

Two renders of the same inputs write the same bytes. Many projects ignore
`.quarto/` in version control, so a record is not something to commit; do not
expect it to be shared between collaborators until a durable use for it
exists.

## What an edit does to a record

Quarto compares a record with the document to decide whether it still
describes it:

| You edit                                             | The record is |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| prose outside cells and spans                        | still fresh   |
| the code in a cell                                   | stale         |
| a `#|` option line                                   | stale         |
| an inline expression                                 | stale         |
| a front matter key that affects execution            | stale         |

So correcting a typo in a paragraph does not re-run your cells in the preview
or in hub. Any other edit above does.

The preview also keeps a cache of its own, keyed on the whole input. A prose
edit can therefore still cause a re-run there for reasons unrelated to the
record; the table is about the record only.

## Positron's cache is a different file

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) keeps its own cache of Quarto outputs,
in per-user storage. Quarto does not use or write that file as its record,
for three reasons: Positron's file is rewritten from a fixed set of fields, so
extra information in it is dropped; it is named after a hash of the document's
location, which Quarto cannot reproduce; and it carries a timestamp that
changes on every write, so its bytes are never stable.

`q2 render` does not read Positron's cache. Only a preview or `q2 provide-hub`
does, and only when you ask for it with `--records positron` (or a directory
of Positron cache files), described next. Quarto never writes to or deletes
Positron's cache. Output shown from it is marked as generated, so the viewer
does not offer to edit it; see
[Outputs from an imported record](../projects/preview.qmd#outputs-from-an-imported-record).

To go the other way and give Positron a cache file built from a document's
record, use [`q2 convert`](convert.qmd).

## Choosing where a preview gets records

`q2 preview` and `q2 provide-hub` take `--records`, a list of the places to
look for a document's record, in order. The first place that has a record for
the document wins; records are never merged.

| Entry | Where the record comes from |
|---|---|
| `cache` | the preview's own cache of earlier runs (`q2 preview` only) |
| `q2` | the copy under `.quarto/execution-records/` that `record: true` writes |
| `positron` | Positron's inline output cache, read without starting a kernel |
| a directory path | a directory of Positron-format cache files |
| `engine` | run the code |

Write the list with commas (`--records cache,q2,engine`) or repeat the flag.
A directory path needs a path separator or a leading `./`, `../`, `/` or `~`;
a bare word that is not one of the names is an error, so write `./notes` for a
directory called `notes`. A directory must exist when the command starts, a
relative path is taken from the directory you run the command in, and a path
that contains a comma cannot be given.

The defaults differ. `q2 preview` uses `cache,q2,engine`: it reuses an earlier
run, then a saved record, and runs the code only if neither has one.
`q2 provide-hub` uses `engine` alone, which is a fresh run each time, after you
approve it. Leave `engine` out and the command never runs code: a preview shows
only the records it finds, and says on the page why each place had none.
`--records` cannot be combined with `--join`, `--static` or `--no-project`, and
`cache` is not available for `provide-hub`.

"Never run code" means no code cell, inline expression or engine process runs.
Your document's filters, shortcodes and includes still run, as in any preview,
and so do the project's pre-render scripts, once, when the preview starts. A
guest of a shared preview can re-run code only when `engine` is in the list and
`preview.engine` is not `off` (under `off`, `engine` in the list is ignored with
a warning).

Two things to know about `provide-hub`. A record from `q2`, `positron` or a
directory is published to everyone viewing the hub document **without** the
approval prompt, because no code runs; naming the source is how you choose to
share those outputs. And until the hosted hub can read records, publishing one
needs `QUARTO_ENGINE_RECORD_WRITE=1` in the environment; without it the record
is refused with a message that names the variable.

The preview reads its sources when it starts, not again when a file changes. A
Positron cache written after the preview started, or a new `.qmd` file, is not
seen until you restart it. With a persisted `--data-dir`, a document that was
re-run keeps the record of that run across restarts, and "Clear results" in
the editor removes a record for every collaborator without looking at the
list again.

## Limits

- A document that uses an engine that builds no execution record is stored in
  the older format. Every output is still shown, but features that read
  records may not work with it.
- A preview that keeps its data with `--data-dir` stores execution records
  there. If you later open that directory with an older version of `q2`, the
  page shows "Failed to parse capture". Use a new `--data-dir`, or delete the
  old one: the older version records the file again. Edits made in the
  `--ui editor` session are not written to your files unless you pass
  `--allow-edit`, so save anything you want to keep first.
- A record from a knitr document can be exported with
  [`q2 convert`](convert.qmd), and a preview reads Positron's outputs for its R
  cells. Cells in other languages of a knitr document do not take outputs from
  Positron's cache.
- To run cells in a kernel other than Python, see
  [Running other languages with Jupyter kernels](jupyter-kernels.qmd), which
  also covers choosing a kernel and what happens when one is missing.
- Inline expressions are described in
  [Inline expressions](computations.qmd#inline-expressions).
